title: How a property lookup is resolved
summary: One loop over an ordered list of sources, returning the first hit. Short enough to read in full, and it settles every precedence question you will ever have.
entry: Put a breakpoint in PropertySourcesPropertyResolver.getProperty and call environment.getProperty("anything"). The loop you land in is the entire mechanism.

steps.notice: The loop. Iterate the sources in order, return on the first non-null. There is no merging, no priority arithmetic and no special casing; precedence is just list order. Read this once and you never have to guess again.

How that order is built. addFirst, addLast, addBefore and addAfter are the whole API, and Boot calls them in a fixed sequence at startup. Anything that wants to win a lookup has to get itself nearer the front.
The one source with special name handling. It maps MY_APP_TIMEOUT onto my.app.timeout, and only here - which is why the same spelling in an ordinary properties file resolves to nothing.

Placeholders are resolved on read, not on load. That is why ${a.b} in one file can point at a value defined in a completely different source, and why a placeholder can resolve differently depending on when it is asked.
